2.q: what was evil in the sight of Yahweh
2.note: Here Yahweh’s “sight” refers to how he judges or decides on the value of something. See how you translated a similar phrase in 2 Chronicles 14:2. Alternate translation: [things that Yahweh said were evil] or [the things that Yahweh considers evil]
Another possible meaning is “including the disgusting things.”

3.q: he rebuilt the high places … he built altars … he made Asherah poles
3.note: Manasseh would have commanded his workers to do the building for him. Alternate translation: [he had the high places rebuilt … he had altars built … he had Asherah poles made] or [he had his workers rebuild the high places … he had them build altars … he had them make Asherah poles]

4.q: It is in Jerusalem that my name will be forever
4.note: The name is a metonym for the person. Alternate translation: [Jerusalem is where I will forever make known who I am]

5.q: He built altars for all the stars of heaven in the two courtyards of the house of Yahweh
5.note: It is implied that he built these altars so people could make sacrifices and worship the stars. Also, he would not have built these altars himself, rather he would have commanded his workers to do it. Alternate translation: [He had his workers build altars in the two courtyards of the house of Yahweh so that the people could worship the stars and offer them sacrifices] (See also: [Metonymy](ta:figs-metonymy))

6.note: This is the name of a place near Jerusalem that is also known as Gehenna.

6.q: he caused his sons to pass through the fire
6.note: You may need to make explicit why he put his son in the fire and what happened after he did so. Alternate translation: [he burned his sons to death as an offering to his gods]
This refers to dead people. Alternate translation: [dead people] or [those who are dead]

6.q: Manasseh did much evil in the sight of Yahweh
6.note: Here Yahweh’s “sight” refers to how he judges or decides on the value of something. See how you translated a similar phrase in 2 Chronicles 14:2. Alternate translation: [Manasseh did many things that Yahweh said were evil] or [He practiced the things that Yahweh considered evil]
Alternate translation: [Manasseh made Yahweh very angry]

7.note: Manasseh probably did not do the work. His servants would have done the work. Alternate translation: [Manasseh had ordered his servants to make]

7.q: that I will put my name forever
7.note: Here God is represented by his “name.” Alternate translation: [where I want people to worship me forever]

8.q: that I assigned to their ancestors
8.note: Alternate translation: [that I gave to their ancestors]

9.q: Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem
9.note: Here “Jerusalem” is a part of “Judah.” Alternate translation: [the people of Judah and Jerusalem]

9.q: even more than the nations that Yahweh had destroyed before the people of Israel
9.note: Here “nations” refers to the people who had lived in the land of Canaan before the Israelites had arrived. Alternate translation: [even more than the people whom Yahweh had destroyed as the people of Israel advanced through the land]

11.note: Yahweh sent the army to attack Jerusalem. Alternate translation: [brought about an attack on them by]

11.q: the commanders of the army of the king of Assyria
11.note: The commanders were accompanied by their soldiers. Alternate translation: [the commanders of the army of the king of Assyria and their soldiers]

11.q: took Manasseh in chains, bound him with fetters, and took him off to Babylon
11.note: Here Manasseh being taken as a prisoner is represented by him being bound by chains and fetters. Fetters were chains placed around the feet. Alternate translation: [seized Manasseh, bound him in chains, and took him as a prisoner to Babylon]

13.q: He prayed to him; and God was begged by him
13.note: The second phrase intensifies the first phrase and emphasizes the earnestness of Manasseh’s prayer. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [He prayed to God and begged him] (See also: [Active or Passive](ta:figs-activepassive))
Alternate translation: [to rule again as king]

14.q: Manasseh built … He surrounded … and raised … He put
14.note: Manasseh did not do the building and construction himself, rather, he commanded his workers to do it. Alternate translation: [Manasseh commanded his workers to build … They surrounded … and raised … He commanded his workers to put]
This was the name of a spring and a stream. See how you translated the “waters of Gihon” in 2 Chronicles 32:30. Alternate translation: [the waters of Gihon]
Translate the name of this hill as you did in 2 Chronicles 27:3.
This refers to cities with walls around them.

15.q: He took away … he had built … and threw
15.note: Manasseh did not do the building and construction himself; rather, he commanded his workers to do it. Alternate translation: [Manasseh commanded his workers to take away … they had previously built … and to throw]
Alternate translation: [the false gods from other countries]

16.note: Manasseh did not do the building and construction himself, rather, he commanded his workers to do it. Alternate translation: [He commanded them to rebuild]
Here “Judah” refers to the people who live there. Alternate translation: [he commanded the people of Judah]

18.q: behold, they are written among the deeds … of Israel
18.note: Alternate translation: [anyone can look among the deeds … Israel and see that they are written there]
These phrases can be stated in active form. Alternate translation: [men have written them]

18.q: the deeds of the kings of Israel
18.note: This in account of the history of Israel that no longer exists.

19.q: the places where he had built high places and set up the Asherah poles and the carved figures
19.note: Manasseh did not do the building and construction himself, rather, he commanded his workers to do it. Alternate translation: [the place where he had the high places built and the Asherah poles and the carved figures set up] or [the places where he commanded his workers to build the high places and to set up the Asherah poles and carved figures]
This is a book that no longer exists.
These phrases can be stated in active form. Alternate translation: [men have written about them]

20.q: So Manasseh slept with his ancestors
20.note: This is a euphemism. Alternate translation: [So Manasseh died]
This is the name of a man.
This is an idiom. Alternate translation: [became the next king] or [became the king of Judah]

22.q: what was evil in the sight of Yahweh
22.note: Here Yahweh’s “sight” refers to how he judges or decides on the value of something. See how you translated a similar phrase in 2 Chronicles 14:2. Alternate translation: [things that Yahweh said were evil] or [the things that Yahweh considers evil]

23.q: this same Amon trespassed more and more
23.note: Alternate translation: [Amon sinned again and again] or [Amon continued to sin]

24.note: This is an idiom. Alternate translation: [killed him]
Alternate translation: [planned in secret to kill him]

25.note: This is an idiom. Alternate translation: [became the next king] or [became the king of Judah]
